CacheView.description: The result cache's counts and pins.

answers.description: Entries holding a whole answer's serialised bytes, in one format.

capacity.description: The budget in bytes (`budgets.result_cache`); 0: the cache is off.

hits.description: Query parts answered from the cache.

misses.description: Query parts computed that could have been cached.

rejected.description:
Parts not kept: cheaper to recompute than to keep, too large, or worth less than
what they would have evicted.

shared.description: Query parts taken from another query computing them at the same time.

ChangeRecord.description: One change of the state, as its history keeps it.

added.description: The statements it added and removed (N-Triples, in the state graph).

DefaultGraphRight.description: A role's right on the store's default graph.

axioms.description: The axioms, each in the functional-style syntax with the triples it was read from.

minimal.description: No axiom can be left out (false: a budget ran out first; the set still entails it).

tests.description: Entailment tests run by the DL engines.

verified.description: A fresh entailment test confirmed the set.

DraftCapabilities.description: What this server's draft checks offer.

max_seconds.description: The longest time limit a request may ask for, in seconds.

semantics.description: What the checks mean; a change of meaning gets a new identifier.

DraftCheckReply.description: The check's terminal answer with the request's identity.

DraftCheckRequest.description:
One check: its identity, its limits and its pinned inputs (N-Triples; the query as
SPARQL text).

input_hashes.description:
SHA-256 of the inputs: `@active_data`, `@active_schema`, `@active_shapes` and
`@query` are verified; others are echoed.

oneOf.description:
Under `owl2-dl`, for a statement the rules don't derive but OWL 2 DL entails: a
minimal set of the ontology's axioms it follows from (`steps` is then empty).

steps.description: The statement first; each premise after the steps that use it.

origin.description: `asserted`, `inferred`, or `hidden` (asserted in no graph the requester may read).

premises.description: The steps (indexes) it is derived from.

rule.description: The rule that derives it, for an inferred step.

subject.description: The statement's terms; left out for a `hidden` step.

Fallback.description: What a role grants a user no rule names, when enforcement is on.

graph.description: The graph's IRI (a blank node in N-Triples form); absent for the default graph.

examples.description: The first quarantined statements in the files' order: where, and why.

load.description: The load's id in the quarantine, if it quarantined any.

quarantined.description: Statements quarantined for syntax errors (the repository's quarantine).

oneOf.description: The inferences recomputed after the load, where the repository reasons.

skipped.description: The same count, by its older name.

Inferred.description: Whether users who may not read every graph see the inferred statements.

description.description: What it works on (the files of an import).

files_done.description: Files done and in all, statements parsed so far.

started.description: When it started, in seconds since the Unix epoch, and how long it ran.

Level.description: A member's level in a workspace.

enforced.description: Whether access is restricted at all.

oneOf.description: Its personal space, where it has a user name.

reads_everything.description: Whether the requester reads every graph (in the repository asked about).

bytes.description: What it takes of the cache's budget.

revision.description:
The revision its result is held for; absent if it isn't held now (the store
changed: the result is pinned again the next time the query runs).

Problem.description:
An error, as every endpoint reports one (RFC 9457 problem details,
`application/problem+json`).

reasoner_reject.description:
For a rejected commit (type `reasoner-reject`, `shacl-reject` or `commit-reject`):
the violated rule or constraint and the statements it shows, where there are any. The
name is kept for every kind, so that clients that read it go on working.

request_id.description: The request's id, as in the `x-request-id` header and the server's log.

QuarantineExample.description: A quarantined statement as a load reports it.

QueryDraft.description: What a client sends to save a query.

QueryForm.description:
A query sent as a form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`): every parameter in the
body, none in the URL.

violations.description: The consistency violations found: 0 exactly when the data is consistent.

violations_at_least.description: Their list stopped at its memory budget: `violations` is a lower bound.

lag_revisions.description: Revisions this replica is behind the primary, as last seen.

last_contact_unix.description: When the primary last answered, seconds since 1970.

last_error.description: What went wrong at the last attempt, if it did.

primary_revision.description: The primary's latest revision when last asked (a replica's).

records_applied.description: Records applied since this server started.

path.description: The path of its engine API.

unavailable.description:
Set when it didn't open at start (its stored settings or files can't be read): it
answers 503 until repaired or removed. Operators see why, with the file and the
repair; others only that it is unavailable.

RepositoryRules.description:
A repository's user rules: their text, kept with the settings so that a restart needs
no file.

name.description: Shown in errors and diagnostics: the file name, or `configuration`.

RepositorySettings.description:
What a repository is created with besides the server's settings. Unknown fields are
refused: a misspelt setting would otherwise be silently ignored.

ql_rewriting.description:
When queries get OWL 2 QL answers through existentials (`auto`, `on`, `off`;
docs/design/ql-rewriting.md §4); the server's `reasoner.ql_rewriting` when absent.

query_timeout_ms.description:
How long one query on this repository may run, in milliseconds; the server's
query timeout when absent. Lets one server hold datasets with different budgets,
e.g. a small one answering an application in seconds beside a large public one.
Applies to repositories other than the default, which keeps the server's.

reader_corpus_bytes.description:
Bytes a `reader` search scope's corpora may take
([`crate::StoreConfig::reader_corpus_bytes`]); the server's
`store.reader_corpus_bytes` when absent.

reasoning.description: The repository's reasoning, by mode name; the server's when absent.

oneOf.description: The repository's user rules, if it has any.

search_scope.description:
What searches rank and select among (`global`, `reader`;
[`crate::StoreConfig::search_scope`]); the server's `store.search_scope` when absent.

oneOf.description: The settings it was created with (none for the default repository: the server's).

service.description: Whether the role's users may call other endpoints with `SERVICE`.

RoleRule.description: A role's graphs: entries are IRIs, or IRI prefixes ending in `*`.

deny.description: Graphs the role's users may neither read nor write, whatever other roles grant.

service.description:
Whether the role's users may call other endpoints with `SERVICE` (a privilege of its
own: it makes the server fetch URLs). Administrators and unrestricted users may.

origin.description: Who sent it, where the caller said.

started.description: When it started, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

name.description: Its name in the space: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

repository.description: The repository it is meant for; absent: any.

space.description: Its space: a personal space (`~alice`) or a workspace.

name.description: Its path in the import directory, with `/`.

files.description: Paths in the import directory (as listed).

graph.description: The graph for triple formats; the default graph without.

enforced.description:
Whether access is restricted at all; off, everyone reads and writes what its
credentials allow.

min_password_length.description: The shortest password a local login takes.

session_hours.description: How long a local login's session lasts, in hours.

users_create_workspaces.description: Whether users who aren't administrators may create workspaces (they own them).

SparqlForm.description:
A query or an update sent as a form to the combined endpoint: exactly one of `query`
(with [`QueryForm`]'s parameters) or `update` (with [`UpdateForm`]'s); both, or neither,
is a 400.

UpdateForm.description: An update sent as a form: every parameter in the body, none in the URL.

password.description: A local login's password; empty removes it. Users set their own.

local_login.description: Whether it has a password for local logins.

graphs.description: Graphs it takes in besides its prefix (administrators only).
Graphs it takes in besides its prefix.

oneOf.description: The requester's level, where it is a member.

repository.description: The repository it is in; absent: every repository.

info.description: Every capability of the engine, the same for every repository (ADR-0007), and users, workspaces and graph policies (ADR-0008). Errors are problem details (`application/problem+json`). The standard protocols (SPARQL 1.1/1.2 Protocol, Graph Store Protocol, RDF4J REST) are served as well; this describes the engine API's routes.

post.summary:
Bulk-loads the RDF document in the body (its format from `Content-Type`): into the
graph `graph` for triple formats (the default graph without), replacing the
repository's statements with `replace=true`. Statements with syntax errors go into the
repository's quarantine, or stop the load with `invalid=strict` (the repository's
`store.invalid_statements` without). Then the inferences are recomputed. For large loads: the
loader's parallel path, not one commit's; administrators only, since a bulk load
replaces whole indexes and passes no commit gate.
